interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is reported absent. Positive surgical margins is documented. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 58.90 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 47.12–70.68 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology revealed a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) and pathological T2 stage with positive surgical margins. Countervailing findings include the absence of extraprostatic extension, no invasion of the seminal vesicles, absence of lymphovascular invasion, and no lymph node metastasis, as documented in the surgical pathology report. The biopsy showed a Gleason 3+3 (ISUP grade group 1) in the peripheral zone. The absence of documented postoperative PSA means biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. The pNx status does not establish node-negative disease, and missing nodal sampling widens uncertainty regarding regional disease control. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory is crucial for revising the prognosis.
